name: Baked Cocoa-Nut Custard
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: powdered white sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of powdered white sugar

ingredients.name: milk of the cocoa-nut or a pint of cream
ingredients.originalText: milk of the cocoa-nut or a pint of cream

ingredients.name: powdered nutmeg and cinnamon
ingredients.originalText: a tea-spoonful of powdered nutmeg and cinnamon

instructions.text: Grate as much cocoa-nut as will weigh a pound
Mix half a pound of powdered white sugar with the milk of the cocoa-nut, or with a pint of cream; adding two table-spoonfuls of rose water
Stir in gradually a pint of rich milk
Beat to a stiff froth the whites of eight eggs, and stir them into the milk and sugar, a little at a time, alternately with the grated cocoa-nut
Add a tea-spoonful of powdered nutmeg and cinnamon
Put the mixture into cups, and bake them twenty minutes in a Dutch oven half filled with boiling water
When cold, grate loaf-sugar over them

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Grate as much cocoa-nut as will weigh a pound
2. Mix half a pound of powdered white sugar with the milk of the cocoa-nut, or with a pint of cream; adding two table-spoonfuls of rose water
3. Stir in gradually a pint of rich milk
4. Beat to a stiff froth the whites of eight eggs, and stir them into the milk and sugar, a little at a time, alternately with the grated cocoa-nut
5. Add a tea-spoonful of powdered nutmeg and cinnamon
6. Put the mixture into cups, and bake them twenty minutes in a Dutch oven half filled with boiling water
7. When cold, grate loaf-sugar over them
